question.text: Nilgiri Multi-Strategy Fund projects FCFF for year 6 (T+1) of INR 200 crore for investee Gamma Ltd. WACC is 12%, terminal growth rate is 5%. What is the terminal value at end of year 5?

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the chapter formula, TV = FCF(T+1) / (WACC - g) = 200 / (0.12 - 0.05) = 200 / 0.07 = INR 2,857.14 crore. This Gordon-growth terminal-value approach is what the DCF example in the chapter illustrates. The Trap: INR 1,666.67 crore uses FCF / WACC and ignores growth; INR 1,400 crore divides by (WACC + g) incorrectly; INR 4,000 crore mis-applies the denominator. Note: The terminal value sits at the end of the explicit-forecast horizon (year 5 here) and uses the next-period free cash flow (year 6) in the numerator.
